title: Leon René, songwriter, and her aunt Augusta Glover
summary: She describes Leon and Otis René as successful songwriters and her aunt Augusta Glover wanting her to meet Leon.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: get excited, I wasn't excited, you know, because I had been promised -- I had had interviews and I had spoken to people and been recommended to people. But none of this happened -- it didn't happen when I expected it to happen. You understand what I'm saying? So for instance, one guy who is a friend of mine, Leon Rainey. You know the René brothers, Leon and Otis René?

Well, Leon and Otis were very successful, you know, musicians. They wrote some wonderful things. Leon, incidentally, wrote that swallows, "The Swallows Come Back to Capistrano," and they wrote, "Sleepy Time Down South," and I think Clarence Muse (INSONIC) got in on that, but they were, I think, the real writers of it, you know. But Clarence did it and featured it and, you know, sold it for them. So -- he gets credit for that, you know. But -- (Recording interruption)
Okay, you were talking about the René brothers. Go on.

Leon and Otis René, were very marvelous musicians, song writers. And very successful, very successful. They did, "Sleepy Time Down South," and they did -- in later years Leon, I think -- I don't know if the both of them wrote it, but I know Leon wrote Swallows, "When the Swallows Come Back to Capistrano," and many other things, marvelous things. And I remember my aunt, Augusta Glover, who was my husband's aunt,

really, well, she was a very close friend to the Renéys, and she admired them greatly, and they lived in her neighborhood. She happened to have been a dear friend to Leon's wife. They worked at PTAs and things together, and they later got me involved in all of that also. But anyway, my aunt said to me, she says, "You know, I'm -- I want Mr. René, I want you to meet Mr. René, Mr. Leon Renéey." So they lived --
